items.title: South Korea Moves to End Its 7-Year ICO Ban
points: South Korea implemented a broad ICO (Initial Coin Offering—a fundraising method where companies sell new cryptocurrencies to investors) ban in 2017 after high-profile fraud cases; the government now plans to lift restrictions and create a regulated framework.
New regulations will likely include investor protections, disclosure requirements, and registration processes for projects seeking domestic token fundraising.
The reversal reflects growing recognition that blanket bans push legitimate projects overseas while hindering domestic blockchain innovation.

South Korea's move could influence other Asian markets to adopt clearer ICO frameworks rather than outright prohibitions, signaling a broader shift from early regulatory overreach toward more nuanced, risk-based crypto oversight.

items.title: CFTC Allows Crypto to Count Toward Derivatives Platform Capital Requirements
points: CFTC staff advisory clarifies that bitcoin, ether, and payment stablecoins (cryptocurrencies pegged to stable assets like the US dollar, used for transfers) can count toward the one-year operating cost coverage component of financial resources requirements for derivatives platforms.
Firms must still maintain separate cash or highly liquid securities to satisfy liquidity requirements—crypto cannot fully replace traditional capital reserves.
The advisory provides regulatory clarity on native asset holdings without requiring a full rulemaking cycle.

items.title: Ethereum Foundation Doubles Security Team for Post-Quantum Upgrade
points: EF doubled its protocol security team, citing AI as a greater near-term risk than quantum computing since AI models now find production bugs faster than humans can review them.

Targeting December 2028 (community goal) with a 2029 internal deadline and January review, to replace vulnerable elliptic curve encryption with hash-based signatures (a quantum-resistant cryptographic method).

Three planned changes: hash-based validator keys for consensus, a migration path to hash-based wallet signatures, and hash-based blob commitments; EF warns the upgrade is harder than the Merge and will require updates to BLS tooling, wallets, multisigs, and staking pools.

items.title: Cross River Bank Launches Bitcoin-Backed Lending
points: Loans up to $250K offered at 30-70% loan-to-value ratios.
Adds FDIC-insured competition to the existing crypto lending market.

items.title: Monad and Stellar Mark Milestones
points: Monad hits $82M weekly tokenized equities volume (up 90% week-over-week) and 885 hackathon teams after one year on mainnet; Visa added it to its stablecoin settlement program and MetaMask runs Money Account services on it.
Stellar's Protocol 30 ('Bell') introduces muxed contract addresses using 64-bit IDs to consolidate customer funds into a single smart account instead of one contract per customer.

Stellar adds native verification of NIST's ML-DSA post-quantum signatures (a cryptographic algorithm resistant to quantum computer attacks) and moves ledger timing to millisecond precision, paving the way for block times below the current 5-second baseline; network signatures remain Ed25519 but indexers must update XDR definitions.
